content.prompt:
The sum of the ages of two children is 24 and the difference between their ages is 8.
If Nikki is the older sister of Travis, determine their ages by setting up and solving a pair of simultaneous equations.

answer.worked: Let $n$ be Nikki’s age and $t$ be Travis’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}n+t&=24 &&(1)\\n-t&=8 &&(2)\end{align*}$$

(1) + (2):
$$\begin{align*}2n&=32\\n&=16\end{align*}$$
Substitute $n=16$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}16+t&=24\\t&=8\end{align*}$$

answer.short: Nikki is 16 years old and Travis is 8 years old.
answer.worked: Nikki is 16 years old and Travis is 8 years old.

sourceReview.taughtMethod: Follow the four numbered modelling steps; add the sum and difference equations, then substitute.

content.prompt: The perimeter of a rectangle is 56 cm. If the length of the rectangle is three times its breadth, determine the dimensions by setting up and solving two simultaneous equations.

answer.short: Let $l$ be the length and $b$ be the breadth, both in centimetres.
answer.worked: Let $l$ be the length and $b$ be the breadth, both in centimetres.
$$\begin{align*}2l+2b&=56\qquad (1)\\l&=3b\qquad (2)\end{align*}$$

Substitute (2) into (1).
$$\begin{align*}2(3b)+2b&=56\\8b&=56\\b&=7\end{align*}$$
Substitute $b=7$ into (2).
$$\begin{align*}l&=3(7)\\l&=21\end{align*}$$
The rectangle is 21 cm long and 7 cm wide.

content.prompt: Adult concert tickets cost $\$5$ more than child tickets. Two adult tickets and two child tickets cost $\$70$ in total. Find the cost of each ticket.

answer.short: Let $a$ be the adult ticket cost and $c$ be the child ticket cost, both in dollars.
answer.worked: Let $a$ be the adult ticket cost and $c$ be the child ticket cost, both in dollars.
$$\begin{align*}a-c&=5\qquad (1)\\2a+2c&=70\qquad (2)\end{align*}$$

Multiply (1) by 2.
$$\begin{align*}2a-2c&=10\qquad (3)\end{align*}$$
Add (2) and (3).
$$\begin{align*}4a&=80\\a&=20\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=20$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}20-c&=5\\c&=15\end{align*}$$
Each child ticket costs $\$15$ and each adult ticket costs $\$20$.

inlines.text: John buys three daffodils and five petunias from the nursery and pays $25.
Julia buys four daffodils and three petunias for $26.
Determine the cost of each type of flower.

answer.worked:
Let $d$ be the cost of one daffodil and $p$ the cost of one petunia, in dollars.
$$\begin{align*}3d+5p&=25 &&(1)\\4d+3p&=26 &&(2)\\12d+20p&=100 &&4\times(1)\\12d+9p&=78 &&3\times(2)\\11p&=22 &&\text{subtract}\\p&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute $p=2$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}3d+5(2)&=25\\3d&=15\\d&=5\end{align*}$$
Each petunia costs $\$2$ and each daffodil costs $\$5$.

inlines.text: Alex buys 4 bolts and 6 washers for $2.20 and Holly spends $1.80 on 3 bolts and 5 washers at the same local hardware store. Determine the costs of each bolt and each washer.

answer.worked:
Let $b$ be the cost of one bolt and $w$ the cost of one washer, in dollars.
$$\begin{align*}4b+6w&=2.20 &&(1)\\3b+5w&=1.80 &&(2)\\12b+18w&=6.60 &&3\times(1)\\12b+20w&=7.20 &&4\times(2)\\2w&=0.60 &&\text{subtract}\\w&=0.30\end{align*}$$
Substitute $w=0.30$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}4b+6(0.30)&=2.20\\4b&=0.40\\b&=0.10\end{align*}$$
Each bolt costs $\$0.10$ and each washer costs $\$0.30$.

inlines.text: A scientist mixes a 10% saline solution with a 30% saline solution to produce 200 mL of a 25% saline solution. Find the volume of each solution used.

answer.short: 50 mL of the 10% solution and 150 mL of the 30% solution.
answer.worked:
Using the variables in the hint, the total volume is 200 mL and the volume of salt is $0.25\times200=50$ mL.
$$\begin{align*}x+y&=200 &&(1)\\0.10x+0.30y&=50 &&(2)\\0.10x+0.10y&=20 &&0.10\times(1)\\0.20y&=30 &&\text{subtract from (2)}\\y&=150\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y=150$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}x+150&=200\\x&=50\end{align*}$$
Use 50 mL of the 10% solution and 150 mL of the 30% solution.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Jack is 5 times as old as his daughter. In 10 years’ time, he will be 3 times her age.

answer.short: Jack is 50 years old and his daughter is 10 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $j$ be Jack’s age and $d$ his daughter’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}j&=5d &&(1)\\j+10&=3(d+10) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}5d+10&=3d+30\\2d&=20\\d&=10\\j&=50\end{align*}$$
Jack is 50 years old and his daughter is 10 years old.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Ben is 3 times as old as his sister Cara. 4 years ago, he was 5 times her age.

answer.short: Ben is 24 years old and Cara is 8 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $b$ be Ben’s age and $c$ Cara’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}b&=3c &&(1)\\b-4&=5(c-4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}3c-4&=5c-20\\16&=2c\\c&=8\\b&=24\end{align*}$$
Ben is 24 years old and Cara is 8 years old.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Lena is 18 years older than Sam. In 6 years’ time, she will be twice his age.

answer.short: Lena is 30 years old and Sam is 12 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $l$ be Lena’s age and $s$ Sam’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}l&=s+18 &&(1)\\l+6&=2(s+6) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}s+24&=2s+12\\s&=12\\l&=30\end{align*}$$
Lena is 30 years old and Sam is 12 years old.

content.prompt:
All the rectangles below are congruent.
They are placed on a coordinate grid and two points as shown.
How long and wide are the rectangles?

$2L+W=11$, $L=4$.

spec.description: Three unshaded congruent rectangles: a horizontal left rectangle and a vertical central rectangle share their bottom baseline; the horizontal right rectangle shares the central rectangle's top baseline. Two marked outer corners retain their coordinate labels. No axes or grid lines are added.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal displacement between marked corners is 2L + W = 12 - 1 = 11. The vertical displacement is L = 6 - 2 = 4. Rectangle boundaries use a consistent coordinate model with L = 4 and W = 3, without displaying those dimensions.
spec.answerVisibility: Coordinate labels and marked points are permanent givens. The source's black annotations 2L + W = 11 and L = 4 are provisionally retained in the worked answer pending resolution of their visibility.

answer.worked:
Let $L$ and $W$ be the length and width of each rectangle.

The horizontal and vertical differences between the marked points give
$$\begin{align*}
2L+W &= 12-1 \\
2L+W &= 11 \\
L &= 6-2 \\
L &= 4.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute $L=4$:
$$\begin{align*}
2(4)+W &= 11 \\
W &= 11-8 \\
W &= 3.
\end{align*}$$
Each rectangle is $4\text{ cm}$ long and $3\text{ cm}$ wide.

A food truck at a Brisbane market pays $\$900$ for the stall plus $\$3.50$ for ingredients for every serve.
Each serve sells for $\$10$, but the market keeps 20% of all sales.
Write two equations, one for costs and one for revenue.
Find how many serves must be sold for the food truck to break-even (cost = revenue).

answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the number of serves produced and sold, and let $C$ and $R$ be the cost and revenue in dollars. The truck keeps 80% of each $\$10$ sale, which is $\$8$.
$$\begin{align*}C&=900+3.5n\\R&=8n\end{align*}$$
At break-even, $C=R$.
$$\begin{align*}900+3.5n&=8n\\4.5n&=900\\n&=200\end{align*}$$
The food truck must sell 200 serves to break even.

Let $x$ be Sophie’s current age and $y$ be her son’s current age, in years.

content.prompt: At present, Emma is 24 years older than her daughter. In 8 years’ time she will be 3 times her daughter’s age. What are Emma and her daughter’s present ages?

answer.short: Emma is 28 years old and her daughter is 4 years old.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Emma’s present age and $y$ be her daughter’s present age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x &= y + 24 \qquad (1) \\ x + 8 &= 3(y + 8) \qquad (2)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (1) into (2).
$$\begin{align*}y + 24 + 8 &= 3(y + 8) \\ y + 32 &= 3y + 24 \\ 8 &= 2y \\ y &= 4\end{align*}$$
Substitute $y = 4$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}x &= 4 + 24 \\ x &= 28\end{align*}$$
Emma is 28 years old and her daughter is 4 years old.

content.prompt:
A factory produces items whose costs are $\$1000$ plus $\$10$ for every item.
The factory receives $\$60$ for every item sold.
Write two equations, one for costs and one for revenue.
Find how many items must be sold for the factory to break-even (cost = revenue).

answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the number of items produced and sold, and let $C$ and $R$ be the cost and revenue in dollars.
$$\begin{align*}
C &= 1000 + 10n \\
R &= 60n
\end{align*}$$
At break-even, $C = R$.
$$\begin{align*}
1000 + 10n &= 60n \\
50n &= 1000 \\
n &= 20
\end{align*}$$
The factory must sell 20 items to break even.

3 pencil-top erasers and 2 clips cost $\$2.05$.

5 pencil-top erasers and 3 clips cost $\$3.20$.

What is the cost of 1 pencil-top eraser and what is the cost of 1 clip?

spec.description: Editable schematic pencil-top erasers and clips replace photographic cutouts. Three stacked rows retain erasers on the left and clips on the right, with unit-price question marks in the final row. Carabiner outlines have an open side closed by a paired-line hinged gate, matching the identifying source feature; all six object counts/positions retained.
spec.mathematics: First row: 3 erasers and 2 clips. Second row: 5 erasers and 3 clips. Third row: 1 eraser and 1 clip, each labelled '= ?'.
spec.answerVisibility: Only object counts and question marks are visible; no unit prices are supplied.

answer.worked:
Let $e$ and $c$ be the prices in dollars of one pencil-top eraser and one clip respectively.
$$\begin{align*}3e+2c&=2.05 &&\text{(1)}\\5e+3c&=3.20 &&\text{(2)}\end{align*}$$
Multiply (1) by 3 and (2) by 2.
$$\begin{align*}9e+6c&=6.15\\10e+6c&=6.40\end{align*}$$
Subtract the first equation from the second.
$$\begin{align*}e&=0.25\end{align*}$$
Substitute $e=0.25$ into (1).
$$\begin{align*}3(0.25)+2c&=2.05\\0.75+2c&=2.05\\2c&=1.30\\c&=0.65\end{align*}$$
One pencil-top eraser costs $\$0.25$ and one clip costs $\$0.65$.

content.prompt:
A business has five times as many junior workers as it does senior workers.

If the weekly wage for a senior is $\$800$ and for a junior is $\$600$, find how many of each are employed if the total weekly wage bill is $\$57000$.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the number of senior workers and $j$ be the number of junior workers.

$$\begin{align*}
j &= 5s &&\text{(1)}\\
800s + 600j &= 57000 &&\text{(2)}
\end{align*}$$

Substitute (1) into (2).

$$\begin{align*}
800s + 600(5s) &= 57000\\
800s + 3000s &= 57000\\
3800s &= 57000\\
s &= 15
\end{align*}$$

Substitute $s=15$ into (1).

$$\begin{align*}
j &= 5(15)\\
j &= 75
\end{align*}$$

The business employs 15 senior workers and 75 junior workers.

content.prompt:
Find the original two-digit number in each part.

(Hint: a number can be written in terms of its digits in this way: $35=3(10)+5$; $\overline{ab}=10a+b$, where $\overline{ab}$ denotes the two-digit number.)

children.label: a
children.prompt:
In a two-digit number, the sum of the digits is 11.
When 27 is added to the number, the digits swap positions.
What is the original 2-digit number?

answer.worked:
Let $a$ be the tens digit and $b$ be the units digit.
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=11 &&(1)\\10a+b+27&=10b+a\\27&=9b-9a\\3&=b-a &&(2)\end{align*}$$
(1) + (2):
$$\begin{align*}2b&=14\\b&=7\end{align*}$$
Substitute $b=7$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}a+7&=11\\a&=4\end{align*}$$
The original number is 47. Check: $47+27=74$.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
In a two-digit number, the tens digit is twice the units digit.
When the digits swap positions, the number decreases by 27.
What is the original 2-digit number?

answer.worked:
Let $a$ be the tens digit and $b$ be the units digit.
$$\begin{align*}a&=2b &&(1)\\10a+b-27&=10b+a\\9a-9b&=27\\a-b&=3 &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Substitute (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}2b-b&=3\\b&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute $b=3$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}a&=2(3)\\a&=6\end{align*}$$
The original number is 63. Check: $63-27=36$.

classification.difficultyReason: The hint supplies 10a+b. The student writes two equations, one involving the digit swap, simplifies to a difference of digits and solves. This is a routine but linked procedure with a representation change.

content.prompt:
All the rectangles below are congruent.
They are placed on a coordinate grid and two points as shown.
How long and wide are the rectangles?

answer.worked:
Substitute $L=3W$ into $L+W=8$:
$$\begin{align*}3W+W&=8\\4W&=8\\W&=2\\L&=3(2)\\L&=6\end{align*}$$
Each rectangle is 6 units long and 2 units wide.

classification.difficultyReason: The student must read two marked corners and turn the diagram into two relations. Horizontally the corners are one width plus one length apart, so L+W=8. Vertically the single upright rectangle's length equals three stacked widths, so L=3W. Neither equation is supplied, which makes it harder than the reference where the equations are given directly. Seeing the 3W = L equivalence is a modest reframing. After that it is one substitution into two linear equations with whole-number results. It involves no elimination across two diagrams, so it is easier than the multi-diagram congruent-rectangle systems. It is slightly above a routine word-problem simultaneous-equations question because of the diagram interpretation.

content.prompt: Sophie is 24 years older than her son. Find Sophie’s current age if:

children.label: a
children.prompt: in 4 years’ time, she will be twice her son’s age.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x+4&=2(y+4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+28&=2y+8\\y&=20\\x&=44\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 44 years old.

children.label: b
children.prompt: 4 years ago, she was twice her son’s age.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x-4&=2(y-4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+20&=2y-8\\y&=28\\x&=52\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 52 years old.

children.label: c
children.prompt: in 4 years’ time, she will be twice the age her son was 4 years ago.

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be Sophie’s age and $y$ her son’s age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x&=y+24 &&(1)\\x+4&=2(y-4) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Sub (1) into (2):
$$\begin{align*}y+28&=2y-8\\y&=36\\x&=60\end{align*}$$
Sophie is 60 years old.

Part c, the hardest, requires reading 'twice the age her son was 4 years ago' as mixed time shifts, with +4 on one side and -4 on the other. That is a small extra translation step. The solving is easy, with integer answers and no fractional ratio, so it sits near p50-q27 (39) and below the simultaneous-equation rectangle problems (p46-q15).

Five years ago I was 5 times as old as my son.
In 8 years’ time I will be 3 times as old as my son.
How old am I today?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ be my current age and $y$ be my son’s current age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x-5 &= 5(y-5) \qquad (1)\\x+8 &= 3(y+8) \qquad (2)\end{align*}$$
Rearrange (1) and substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}x-5 &= 5y-25\\x &= 5y-20\\5y-20+8 &= 3(y+8)\\5y-12 &= 3y+24\\2y &= 36\\y &= 18\\x &= 5(18)-20\\x &= 70\end{align*}$$
I am 70 years old today.

Let $x$ be Emily’s current age and $y$ Ally’s current age, in years.
$$\begin{align*}x-4&=2(y-4)\\x+4&=\frac{5}{4}(y+4)\end{align*}$$
Simplifying:
$$\begin{align*}x-2y&=-4 &&(1)\\4x-5y&=4 &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Equation $(2)-4\times(1)$:
$$\begin{align*}3y&=20\\y&=\frac{20}{3}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}x-2\left(\frac{20}{3}\right)&=-4\\x&=\frac{28}{3}\end{align*}$$
Emily is $9\frac{1}{3}$ years old and Ally is $6\frac{2}{3}$ years old.

content.prompt:
Olivia the fruiterer sells two fruit packs.

Pack 1: 10 apples and 5 mangoes ($\$12$).

Pack 2: 15 apples and 4 mangoes ($\$14.15$)

Determine the cost of 1 apple and 5 mangoes.

answer.worked:
Let $a$ be the cost of one apple and $m$ the cost of one mango, in dollars.

$$\begin{align*}10a+5m &= 12 &&\text{(1)}\\15a+4m &= 14.15 &&\text{(2)}\\40a+20m &= 48 &&\text{(1)}\times4\\75a+20m &= 70.75 &&\text{(2)}\times5\\35a &= 22.75 &&\text{subtract}\\a &= 0.65\end{align*}$$

Substitute $a=0.65$ into (1).

$$\begin{align*}10(0.65)+5m &= 12\\6.50+5m &= 12\\5m &= 5.50\\m &= 1.10\end{align*}$$

The cost of 1 apple and 5 mangoes is

$$\begin{align*}a+5m &= 0.65+5(1.10)\\&=\$6.15.\end{align*}$$

spec.mathematics: Left side 3y-x; right side 2+2y; base 5x+3. All three sides are equal.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied side expressions are visible in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
All sides of an equilateral triangle are equal.
$$\begin{align*}
3y-x &= 2+2y \\
y-x &= 2 \qquad (1) \\
3y-x &= 5x+3 \\
3y-6x &= 3 \qquad (2)
\end{align*}$$
From (1), $y=x+2$. Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}
3(x+2)-6x &= 3 \\
3x+6-6x &= 3 \\
-3x &= -3 \\
x &= 1 \\
y &= 1+2 \\
y &= 3
\end{align*}$$
Each side has length $5(1)+3=8$ units.

content.prompt:
A parabola has the equation $y=x^2+2x+3$.
Find the values of $a$ and $c$ in the equation $y=(x-a)^2+c$ and hence determine the coordinates of the vertex $(a,c)$.

answer.worked:
Expand and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}(x-a)^2+c&=x^2-2ax+a^2+c\\-2a&=2\\a&=-1\\a^2+c&=3\\(-1)^2+c&=3\\c&=2\end{align*}$$
The vertex is $(a,c)=(-1,2)$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Given that $a(x+b)^2+c=3x^2-12x+15$ for all $x$, find $a,b$, and $c$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
a(x+b)^2+c&=ax^2+2abx+ab^2+c.
\end{align*}$$
Equating coefficients,
$$\begin{align*}
a&=3\\
2ab&=-12\\
6b&=-12\\
b&=-2\\
ab^2+c&=15\\
3(-2)^2+c&=15\\
c&=3.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $3x^2-12x+15=3(x-2)^2+3$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find the minimum value of $3x^2-12x+15$ and state the value of $x$ at which it occurs.

answer.worked:
Since $(x-2)^2\geq0$,
$$\begin{align*}
3x^2-12x+15&=3(x-2)^2+3\\
&\geq3.
\end{align*}$$
Equality occurs when $(x-2)^2=0$, so $x=2$. The minimum value is $3$. Equivalently, the parabola has its minimum turning point at $(2,3)$.

content.prompt: The minimum value of $x^2-8x+k$ is 3. Find the value of $k$.

answer.worked:
Write $x^2-8x+k=(x+a)^2+c$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-8x+k&=x^2+2ax+a^2+c\\2a&=-8\\a&=-4\\a^2+c&=k\\c&=k-16\end{align*}$$
So $x^2-8x+k=(x-4)^2+k-16$. Since $(x-4)^2\geq0$, the minimum value is $k-16$.
$$\begin{align*}k-16&=3\\k&=19\end{align*}$$

content.prompt: A rectangular prism has width $y$ cm, length $(x+a)$ cm and height $(x+b)$ cm, where $a$ and $b$ are integers and $a>b$.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the surface area of the rectangular prism is given by the expression
$$2y(2x+a+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\text{ cm}^2.$$

answer.worked:
There are two faces of each of the three different areas.
$$\begin{align*}S&=2y(x+a)+2y(x+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\\&=2y\big((x+a)+(x+b)\big)+2(x+a)(x+b)\\&=2y(2x+a+b)+2(x+a)(x+b)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the surface area of the rectangular prism is equivalent to the expression $2y(2x+1)+2x^2+2x-12\text{ cm}^2$, find $a$ and $b$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}S&=2y(2x+a+b)+2\big(x^2+(a+b)x+ab\big)\\&=4xy+2(a+b)y+2x^2+2(a+b)x+2ab\end{align*}$$
Equate the coefficients of $y$ and the constant terms.
$$\begin{align*}2(a+b)&=2\\a+b&=1\\2ab&=-12\\ab&=-6\end{align*}$$
The integers $3$ and $-2$ have sum $1$ and product $-6$. Since $a>b$, $a=3$ and $b=-2$.

content.prompt: The inner radius is $r>0$ and the outer radius is $kr$, where $k>1$. Half the ring is shaded. Find the shaded fraction of the outer circle. Can it ever equal one half? Explain by splitting the numerator.

spec.description: Concentric circles with half the ring shaded. Schematic radii r and kr; k>1.
spec.mathematics: Inner radius r>0, outer radius kr, k>1. Shaded area is half the annulus.

answer.short: $\dfrac{k^2-1}{2k^2}=\dfrac12-\dfrac{1}{2k^2}<\dfrac12$. Since $k>1$, the subtracted term is positive, so it never equals one half.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}}&=\pi(kr)^2=\pi k^2r^2\\A_{\text{shaded}}&=\frac12(\pi k^2r^2-\pi r^2)\\f&=\frac{\frac12\pi r^2(k^2-1)}{\pi k^2r^2}\\f&=\frac{k^2-1}{2k^2}\\f&=\frac{k^2}{2k^2}-\frac1{2k^2}\\f&=\frac12-\frac1{2k^2}\end{align*}$$
For every $k>1$, $\frac1{2k^2}>0$, so the shaded fraction is always less than one half and can never equal it.

content.prompt: Write as a sum of two fractions:

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{6}{(x-1)(x+1)}&=\frac{a}{x-1}+\frac{b}{x+1}\\6&=a(x+1)+b(x-1)\\6&=x(a+b)+(a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=0\quad(1)\\a-b&=6\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and (2):
$$\begin{align*}2a&=6\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=3$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}3+b&=0\\b&=-3\\\frac{6}{(x-1)(x+1)}&=\frac{3}{x-1}-\frac{3}{x+1}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{7}{(x+2)(2x-3)}&=\frac{a}{x+2}+\frac{b}{2x-3}\\7&=a(2x-3)+b(x+2)\\7&=x(2a+b)+(-3a+2b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}2a+b&=0\quad(1)\\-3a+2b&=7\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Twice (1) minus (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=-7\\a&=-1\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=-1$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}-2+b&=0\\b&=2\\\frac{7}{(x+2)(2x-3)}&=-\frac{1}{x+2}+\frac{2}{2x-3}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{-5}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}&=\frac{a}{2x-1}+\frac{b}{3x+1}\\-5&=a(3x+1)+b(2x-1)\\-5&=x(3a+2b)+(a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}3a+2b&=0\quad(1)\\a-b&=-5\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and twice (2):
$$\begin{align*}5a&=-10\\a&=-2\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=-2$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}-2-b&=-5\\b&=3\\\frac{-5}{(2x-1)(3x+1)}&=-\frac{2}{2x-1}+\frac{3}{3x+1}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{9x+4}{(3x-1)(x+2)}&=\frac{a}{3x-1}+\frac{b}{x+2}\\9x+4&=a(x+2)+b(3x-1)\\9x+4&=x(a+3b)+(2a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+3b&=9\quad(1)\\2a-b&=4\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and three times (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=21\\a&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=3$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}6-b&=4\\b&=2\\\frac{9x+4}{(3x-1)(x+2)}&=\frac{3}{3x-1}+\frac{2}{x+2}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{2x-1}{(x+3)(x-4)}&=\frac{a}{x+3}+\frac{b}{x-4}\\2x-1&=a(x-4)+b(x+3)\\2x-1&=x(a+b)+(-4a+3b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=2\quad(1)\\-4a+3b&=-1\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Three times (1) minus (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=7\\a&=1\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=1$ into (1):
$$\begin{align*}1+b&=2\\b&=1\\\frac{2x-1}{(x+3)(x-4)}&=\frac{1}{x+3}+\frac{1}{x-4}\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\frac{1-x}{(2x-1)(4-x)}&=\frac{a}{2x-1}+\frac{b}{4-x}\\1-x&=a(4-x)+b(2x-1)\\1-x&=x(-a+2b)+(4a-b)\end{align*}$$
Comparing coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}-a+2b&=-1\quad(1)\\4a-b&=1\quad(2)\end{align*}$$
Adding (1) and twice (2):
$$\begin{align*}7a&=1\\a&=\frac17\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=\frac17$ into (2):
$$\begin{align*}\frac47-b&=1\\b&=-\frac37\\\frac{1-x}{(2x-1)(4-x)}&=\frac{1}{7(2x-1)}-\frac{3}{7(4-x)}\end{align*}$$

The profit ($P$) is the revenue minus the cost:

content.prompt:
Consider the simultaneous equations.
$$ax + y - 4 = 0$$
$$x + 2y - a = 0$$
If the equations have no real solutions, what is the value of $a$?

$\text{A. }a = \frac{1}{2}$
$\text{B. }a = 1$
$\text{C. }a = 4$
$\text{D. }a = 8$

answer.worked:
For the equations to have no real solutions, the lines must be parallel with different $y$-intercepts.
$$\begin{align*}
ax + y - 4 &= 0 \\
y &= -ax + 4
\end{align*}$$
So $m_1=-a$.
$$\begin{align*}
x + 2y - a &= 0 \\
2y &= -x + a \\
y &= -\frac{x}{2} + \frac{a}{2}
\end{align*}$$
So $m_2=-\frac{1}{2}$. Since the lines are parallel:
$$\begin{align*}
-a &= -\frac{1}{2} \\
a &= \frac{1}{2}
\end{align*}$$
At $a=\frac12$, the lines have equal gradients $-\frac12$, but their $y$-intercepts are $4$ and $\frac a2=\frac14$, which are different. Thus the lines are distinct and parallel and have no simultaneous solution.
Correct answer: A.

Let $p$ be the numerator and $q$ the denominator.

$$\begin{align*}

3p-2q &= -5 \qquad (1) \\

$$\begin{align*}

3p-6p+4 &= -5 \\
-3p &= -9 \\
p &= 3 \\
q &= 3(3)-2 \\
q &= 7
\end{align*}$$

The original fraction was $\frac{3}{7}$.

$$\begin{align*}(x+a)^{2}(x-2)&=(x^{2}+2ax+a^{2})(x-2)\\&=x^{3}+(2a-2)x^{2}+(a^{2}-4a)x-2a^{2}.\end{align*}$$
Equate constant terms and coefficients:
$$\begin{align*}-2a^{2}&=-18\\a^{2}&=9\\a^{2}-4a&=-3\\9-4a&=-3\\a&=3\\b&=2a-2\\b&=2(3)-2\\b&=4.\end{align*}$$

children.prompt: Given that $a(x+b)^2+c=-2x^2+8x-9$ for all $x$, find $a$, $b$, and $c$.

answer.worked:
Expand and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}a(x+b)^2+c&=ax^2+2abx+ab^2+c\\a&=-2\\2ab&=8\\ab^2+c&=-9\end{align*}$$
Substitute $a=-2$.
$$\begin{align*}-4b&=8\\b&=-2\\-2(-2)^2+c&=-9\\c&=-1\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence explain why $-2x^2+8x-9$ is negative for all real values of $x$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}-2x^2+8x-9&=-2(x-2)^2-1\end{align*}$$
For every real $x$,
$$\begin{align*}(x-2)^2&\geq0\\-2(x-2)^2&\leq0\\-2(x-2)^2-1&\leq-1<0\end{align*}$$
Therefore $-2x^2+8x-9$ is negative for all real $x$.

classification.difficultyReason: Model a pursuit with different speeds and a one-hour head start.

content.prompt:
Erin goes off on a long bike ride, averaging 10 km/h.
One hour later her brother Alistair starts chasing after her at 16 km/h.
How long will it take Alistair to catch up to Erin?

answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the time in hours after Alistair starts and $d$ the distance travelled from their starting point in kilometres.

Erin has a one-hour head start:
$$\begin{align*}d&=10(t+1) &&(1)\\d&=16t &&(2)\end{align*}$$
Equating the distances:
$$\begin{align*}10(t+1)&=16t\\10t+10&=16t\\6t&=10\\t&=\frac{5}{3}\end{align*}$$
Alistair catches Erin 1 hour 40 minutes after he starts.

classification.difficultyReason: Model two constant fuel-consumption rates and impose a relationship between the remaining amounts.

content.prompt: Two planes have the same size fuel tanks, but one will travel for 21 hours on a full tank and the other 35 hours on a full tank. They set off at the same time with full tanks and both planes burn fuel at a constant rate. After how long will one have 3 times as much fuel as the other?

answer.worked:
Let A be the plane whose full tank lasts 21 hours and B the plane whose full tank lasts 35 hours. Take each tank's capacity as 105 units, the LCM of 21 and 35. A burns 5 units per hour and B burns 3 units per hour.

Let $t$ be the time in hours and $F_A,F_B$ the remaining fuel amounts.

$$\begin{align*}
F_A &= 105-5t \\
F_B &= 105-3t
\end{align*}$$

B burns fuel more slowly, so set $F_B=3F_A$.

$$\begin{align*}
105-3t &= 3(105-5t) \\
105-3t &= 315-15t \\
12t &= 210 \\
t &= 17.5
\end{align*}$$

After 17.5 hours, B has three times as much fuel as A.

classification.difficultyReason: Construct a sum-of-squares identity and use it to justify non-negativity.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that $5x^2+4x+1$ can be written as $(ax+b)^2+(cx+d)^2$ for some $a,b,c,d$.

answer.worked:
Expanding and equating coefficients gives
$$\begin{align*}
(ax+b)^2+(cx+d)^2&=(a^2+c^2)x^2+(2ab+2cd)x+b^2+d^2\\
a^2+c^2&=5\\
2ab+2cd&=4\\
b^2+d^2&=1.
\end{align*}$$
Choose $b=1$ and $d=0$. Then $2a=4$, so $a=2$, and $c^2=1$. Choose $c=1$.
$$\begin{align*}
(2x+1)^2+x^2&=4x^2+4x+1+x^2\\
&=5x^2+4x+1.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence explain why $5x^2+4x+1$ can never be negative for any real value of $x$.

answer.short: It is the sum of two squared terms, so $5x^2+4x+1\geq0$ for all real $x$.
answer.worked:
For every real $x$, both $(2x+1)^2$ and $x^2$ are non-negative. Therefore
$$\begin{align*}
5x^2+4x+1&=(2x+1)^2+x^2\\
&\geq0.
\end{align*}$$

classification.difficultyReason: Model two opposing journeys using distance from a common reference point.

content.prompt:
Two ancient armies are about to battle each other.
The Egyptians are in town.
The Romans are 1 km away from the town.
The armies begin walking towards each other.
The Egyptians walk at a pace of 3 km/h and the Romans walk at a pace of 4 km/h.
For how long will they walk before the battle begins?
(Hint: let the equations represent distance from the town; $d=st$.)
Give an exact time in hours, or a time in minutes and seconds rounded to the nearest second.

answer.worked:
Let $t$ be the time in hours after both armies start walking and $d$ their distance from town in kilometres.

The Egyptians move away from town; the Romans approach it:
$$\begin{align*}d&=3t &&(1)\\d&=1-4t &&(2)\end{align*}$$
At their meeting point:
$$\begin{align*}3t&=1-4t\\7t&=1\\t&=\frac{1}{7}\end{align*}$$
They walk for $\frac{1}{7}$ hour. This is $\frac{3600}{7}$ seconds, approximately 8 minutes 34 seconds.

Worked example: Mia is 4 times as old as her brother Leo. In 6 years’ time, she will be twice his age.
Find their current ages.
1.	Let $m$ be Mia’s age now and $l$ be Leo’s age now, in years.
2.	In 6 years’ time their ages will be $m+6$ and $l+6$.
$$\begin{align*}m&=4l &&(1)\\m+6&=2(l+6) &&(2)\end{align*}$$
3.	Sub (1) into (2)
$$\begin{align*}4l+6&=2l+12\\4l+6\color{#ef6068}{-2l-6}&=2l+12\color{#ef6068}{-2l-6}\\2l&=6\\l&=3\end{align*}$$
3. (cont.)	Sub $l=3$ into (1)
$$\begin{align*}m&=4(3)\\m&=12\end{align*}$$
4.	Mia is 12 years old and Leo is 3 years old.

Proposed question: Set up and solve a pair of simultaneous equations to find the current ages in each case.
a) Jack is 5 times as old as his daughter. In 10 years’ time, he will be 3 times her age.
b) Ben is 3 times as old as his sister Cara. 4 years ago, he was 5 times her age.
c) Lena is 18 years older than Sam. In 6 years’ time, she will be twice his age.
Answers: a) Jack is 50 years old and his daughter is 10 years old.; b) Ben is 24 years old and Cara is 8 years old.; c) Lena is 30 years old and Sam is 12 years old.

entries.description:
Equilateral: all sides equal.
x + 2y = 5y − x ⇒ 2x − 3y = 0 … (1)
Perimeter: 3(x + 2y) = 42 ⇒ x + 2y = 14
so 3x + 6y = 42 … (2)
From (1): x = (3/2)y. Sub into (2): (9/2)y + 6y = 42
(21/2)y = 42
y = 4
x = 6.

entries.description: Two planes have the same size fuel tanks, but one will travel for 21 hours on a full tank and the other 35 hours on a full tank. entries.description:
Let plane A be plane that uses fuel faster (21 h)
Let plane B be plane that uses fuel slower (35 h)
Let the tank size be 105 units (the LCM of 21 and 35)
Plane A would burn fuel at 5 units per hour
Plane B would burn fuel at 3 units per hour
Fuel remaining in plane A at time t: F_A = 105 − 5t
Fuel remaining in plane B at time t: F_B = 105 − 3t
Set F_B = 3F_A
105 − 3t = 3(105 − 5t)
105 − 3t = 315 − 15t
12t = 210
t = 17.5 hrs

entries.description:

\(ax^2+6ax+9a-bx+5=4x^2+c\)

coefficients of \(x^2\): \(a=4\)
coefficients of \(x\): \(6a-b=0\)
constant terms: \(9a+5=c\)
3. Solve for unknowns

\(6(4)-b=0,\quad b=24\)
\(9(4)+5=c,\quad c=41\)
\(a=4,b=24,c=41\)

entries.expectedAnswer:
4x² − 4x + 2 = (2x − 1)² + 1
So for 4x² − 4x + 2 = k
(2x − 1)² + 1 = k

k ≥ 1
